label: GO WITH CONDITIONS
call: Quote $3,500 (option A) from install #4 in December, once 3 installs close at $2,000 by 2026-11-30 at a 30% close rate on calls held. Cap installs at 2 a month and keep the $500 tier off the price list until its runbook passes a paid test.

why.point: At $2,000 the $5k goal eats 31 to 37 of a 43-hour month; $3,500 needs about 18 to 21 hours.
With tuning counted, $2,000 pays about $121 an hour, 0.8x delivery cost against a 5 to 10x rule.
Three closes at $2,000 in November prove demand first, so a December stall can only be the price.
Record installs 1 to 3; the runbook built from them is the part the founder owns.

minority.quote: At $3,500 you are still renting your time, just at a better rate.
minority.would_have_to_be_true: A stranger can install the plugin from the runbook with 1.5 hours or less of founder time.

next_steps.action: Start the install 1 time log with a weekly ideas count, and screen-record every install.
Log install 1's hours and write the tuning definition of done with the capped guarantee.
Count closes and close rate; if the gate clears, quote $3,500 to the next 10 prospects.

kill_criteria: Under 3 closes by 2026-11-30 keeps $2,000; 0 of 10 closes at $3,500 by 2026-12-31 goes back to $2,000; kill C if its tester needs over 3 founder hours.
conditions: 3 installs close at $2,000 by 2026-11-30, 30% or better of calls held
Tuning capped at 5 hours with three named deliverables and two check-ins
Guarantee: 20 usable ideas a week by day 30, then up to 3 free hours, then a $1,000 partial refund
No more than 2 installs a month at any price

fights.crux: Raise the price before a single install is delivered?
fights.story: Four seats wanted to raise and Graham wanted to hold. Graham moved when the capacity math showed B cannot hit the goal; the others added November's 3 closes as a gate.

fights.crux: Is the $500 self-serve tier leverage now, or a distraction?
fights.story: Naval stood alone for C now. He moved to A now and C later because there is nothing to document yet and no audience to sell to.

fights.crux: Does $2,000 already beat consulting per hour?
fights.story: Graham's $160 an hour left out tuning. Buffett put break-even at 13.3 hours; Graham then showed capacity alone justifies the raise, so the log informs rather than gates.

amendments.amendment: Cap the free-tuning guarantee and add a partial refund.
amendments.reason: Unlimited free tuning cancelled the 5-hour cap; Welsh's 3 hours and Buffett's $1,000 refund used.

amendments.amendment: Cap the guarantee at 3 more hours, and get install 1's day-14 ideas count.
amendments.reason: Adopted with Buffett's refund; the day-14 count is tracked as a measurement, not a gate.

amendments.amendment: Cap installs at 2 a month at any price, and log the weekly ideas count.
Make the hours log an input, not a gate; count close rate per call held.
amendments.reason: Capacity alone justifies the raise at 13 hours, and 3 of 20 messages is only 15%.

amendments.amendment: Raise the December test from 5 prospects to 10.
amendments.reason: Zero closes from 5 quotes happens 17% of the time at a 30% close rate.

amendments.amendment: Tell November prospects now that the price rises on 2026-12-01.
amendments.reason: It commits to the raise before November's gate clears and breaks the control the room agreed.

amendments.amendment: Build the runbook regardless; pass C at 1.5 founder hours, rewrite up to 3, kill above 3.

cheapest_test: Quote $3,500 to the next 10 qualified prospects in December.
revisit: 2027-01-05, with closes and close rate at $3,500, hours per install, the ideas count, and the runbook tester result.
